title: Redis Caching Patterns: Cache-Aside vs Write-Through
learningObjectives: Implement Cache-Aside, Write-Through, and Write-Behind caching strategies
Determine appropriate Time-To-Live (TTL) policies and eviction strategies (LRU, LFU)
Design composite cache keys and namespace invalidation patterns
keyTradeoffs: Read-heavy cache-aside simplicity vs write-through data consistency guarantees
Memory cost of high TTL caches vs database query load on cache misses
commonPitfalls: Setting identical TTLs on thousands of cached keys, causing synchronized mass expiration
Caching null or error responses improperly without a short protective TTL
transferPrompt: What happens when a hot cache key expires while thousands of concurrent requests arrive simultaneously?
